name: Elastomeric vs Acrylic for Los Angeles Stucco Exteriors

mainEntity.name: What are the pros and cons of using elastomeric coatings versus standard acrylic paint on older stucco homes in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What are the pros and cons of using elastomeric coatings versus standard acrylic paint on older stucco homes in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older stucco homes in Los Angeles County often develop hairline cracking and minor movement that owners hope to “seal” with elastomeric coatings. Elastomerics are thick, rubber-like coatings designed to span small cracks, resist wind-driven rain, and create a more uniform surface. On stucco that has many hairline cracks but no active water intrusion from behind, a properly applied elastomeric system can significantly improve appearance and reduce water penetration. However, elastomerics are less vapor permeable than many high-end acrylics, so if moisture is coming from the interior or behind the stucco, they can trap that moisture and contribute to blistering or peeling. They also lock in the texture and color system, making future color changes more laborious because of the thickness and strong adhesion. Premium 100% acrylic exterior paints, by contrast, generally provide excellent UV resistance, color retention, and better breathability for most non-cracked stucco. They handle thermal movement well and are easier to repaint or change colors over time. For homes with isolated cracking, combining targeted elastomeric patching with a high-grade acrylic topcoat often balances performance and flexibility. Discuss your stucco’s age, crack patterns, and any history of moisture issues with a contractor who uses both systems regularly so they can recommend the most appropriate approach.
acceptedAnswer.description: Elastomeric coatings can bridge hairline cracks and improve water resistance on older stucco in Los Angeles County, but they are thicker, less breathable, and harder to change later. High-quality acrylic paint is more breathable and flexible for future repaints but may not hide persistent cracking as well.
